extracted.intended_audience: registered apprenticeship program sponsors, participating employers, Registration Agencies, and public commenters
extracted.subtask_description: Extracts and lists the proposed regulatory requirements for written standards of registered apprenticeship programs (e.g., credential disclosure, wages, safety, ratios, recordkeeping, advanced standing). Intended for sponsors, Registration Agencies, and stakeholders implementing or commenting on apprenticeship program standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interim credentials disclosure (§29.8(a)(8)(i))
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards must include a description of any interim credentials issued to an apprentice during the term of the registered apprenticeship program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is intended to increase transparency so apprentices understand credentials they will receive during participation. Based on existing requirements; Department seeks comments on collecting this information from sponsors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Credential/qualification/licensure upon completion (§29.8(a)(8)(ii))
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards must include any industry-portable occupational qualification, license, credential, or certification that the apprentice receives, or may be eligible to receive, upon completion of the registered apprenticeship program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides transparency about post-program credentials that benefit apprentices; Department is interested in comments and recognizes some programs already provide this information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Postsecondary credit disclosure (§29.8(a)(8)(iii))
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards must include any postsecondary credit that an apprentice receives, or may be eligible to receive, upon completion of the related instruction or on-the-job training components of the program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognizes some programs operate with educational institutions. There would be no requirement to create additional credentials or credits, only to describe any that are provided; aims to support apprentice welfare and informed choice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Related instruction pay disclosure (whether hours counted as work) (§29.8(a)(9))
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards must state whether time spent in related instruction is counted as hours worked, and if so, what the wage rate and any fringe benefits would be for those hours.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Serves as safeguard to ensure sponsors consider payment for related instruction and provides notice to apprentices. Sponsors must comply with Federal, State, or local legal requirements regarding payment for training time (e.g., Fair Labor Standards Act), though sponsors may choose to pay even if not legally required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Process for regular assessment and feedback (§29.8(a)(10))
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards must set forth a process for regularly assessing and providing feedback to the apprentice regarding acquisition of job-related knowledge, skills, and competencies during on-the-job training.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expands on periodic review requirements by requiring an explicit process included in standards, and that feedback be shared with apprentices. Feedback must be inclusive and accessible to all apprentices, including those with disabilities. Intended to tie assessments to work process schedule and apprenticeship term, ensure competency attainment and track wage progression tied to competencies. Allows granting advanced standing for accelerated attainment (see §29.8(a)(20)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of end-point assessments acknowledgment (§29.8(a)(11))
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards must address the utilization of end-point assessments the program uses to determine if an apprentice is fully proficient and eligible to complete the apprenticeship.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposed §29.16 would require administration of an end-point assessment at conclusion of the term and §29.18 maintenance of progress records. End-point assessments validate acquisition of necessary skills and competencies; should be structured to be inclusive to apprentices with disabilities. The standards must acknowledge that §29.16 requirements are met so the process is clear.

rubrics_metrics.name: Probationary period limitation (§29.8(a)(12))
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards must provide for a probationary period that is 'reasonable' and does not exceed 25 percent of the program length or 1 year, whichever is shorter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Retains language from 2008 final rule at §29.5(b)(8).

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance with applicable laws statement (§29.8(a)(13))
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards must include a statement that the registered apprenticeship program will be conducted in accordance with all applicable Federal, State, or local laws.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasizes apprentice safety and welfare; sponsors are responsible for ensuring programs meet requirements for legal work (e.g., state licenses). Noncompliance may subject sponsors to deregistration proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equal worker allowances/rights protections statement (§29.8(a)(14))
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards must state that apprentices are entitled to the same worker allowances, rights, and protections afforded by applicable Federal, State, or local laws to similarly situated non-apprentice employees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Could include family and medical leave, workers' compensation, health and retirement benefits. Does not require apprentices to receive protections beyond what similar non-apprentices would receive. Purpose is transparency and informed choice for potential apprentices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attestation of adequate, safe, and accessible facilities (§29.8(a)(15))
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards must include an attestation that the sponsor will provide adequate, safe, and accessible facilities for training and supervision of apprentices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sponsors should provide documentation where available (e.g., OSHA certifications), though not all sponsors will have such certifications. Accessibility must include individuals with disabilities; examples include nearby bathrooms and lactation facilities, appropriately fitting personal protective equipment. Facilities must comply with applicable laws, including disability, occupational safety, and health laws.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attestation of industry-recognized safety training (§29.8(a)(16))
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards must include an attestation that the sponsor will provide adequate, industry-recognized safety training for apprentices in both on-the-job and related instruction components.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Safety training must be tailored to mitigate potential workplace hazards encountered in the covered occupation (example: electrician programs must address hazards specific to electricians). Expands existing §29.5(b)(9) requirement to further apprentice safety and welfare.

rubrics_metrics.name: Wages and fringe benefits specification (§29.8(a)(17))
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards must include wages and fringe benefits that the apprentice will receive during the registered apprenticeship program, including a progressively increasing schedule of wages and articulation of fringe benefits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entry wage may not be less than the Federal/State/local minimum wage (subject to other laws like Davis-Bacon). 'Fringe benefits' include health insurance, contributions to retirement plans. Proposed additions: graduated wage schedule should increase to reflect progressive acquisition of skills/competencies; include at least one wage progression during first 2,000 hours and reasonable intervals for longer programs; final wage step must be at least 75% of the usual journeyworker wage (with exceptions for prevailing wage or collective bargaining). Purpose: protect apprentices from low/flat wages and support economic mobility. Also reminds sponsors wages must not discriminate per 29 CFR part 30 and apprentices must not be misclassified as independent contractors where they meet employee definitions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program costs transparency and reasonableness (§29.8(a)(18))
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards must disclose the nature and amount of any unreimbursed costs, expenses, or fees an apprentice may incur (e.g., equipment, supplies, books, tuition, assessment fees), and such costs may be charged only if necessary and reasonable, do not impose substantial or inequitable barriers, and comply with applicable law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Addresses risk of financial exploitation and barriers to enrollment/completion. Sponsors must ensure costs imposed by outside parties (e.g., community colleges) do not jeopardize participation. Encourages sponsors to form partnerships or use grants to defray costs. Department seeks comments on whether 'necessary and reasonable' should be more precisely defined (e.g., percentage-of-wages threshold) or left flexible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Apprentice-to-journeyworker ratio (§29.8(a)(19))
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards must address the ratio of apprentices to journeyworkers; the sponsor's ratio must be approved by a Registration Agency and be consistent with safety, health, supervision, and training considerations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Factors to consider include risk of exposure to hazardous conditions, risk of serious injury or death, and health risks from toxic materials. High-hazard industries (defined by BLS fatality rate) may face heightened scrutiny for ratios above 1:1. Ratios should be specific to workforce/workplace/job site/department/plant and consistent with any collective bargaining agreements or laws. Department removed 'continuity of employment' as a factor but solicits comments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advanced standing, credit, and increased wage process (§29.8(a)(20))
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards must grant advanced standing, credit, and an increased wage when appropriate, and include a process to reduce the usual term of on-the-job training or related instruction based on prior qualifications or expedited progress.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The process must be fair, transparent, and objective in identifying, assessing, and documenting prior learning/experience or accelerated progress, and the resulting advanced standing/credit/wage must be commensurate with progression. Examples include military experience, completion of pre-apprenticeship programs, or registered CTE apprenticeship programs. Ensures sponsors retain flexibility while protecting against inappropriate abbreviated training.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transfer of apprentices provision (§29.8(a)(21))
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards must include a provision addressing the transfer of apprentices, carrying forward substantive elements requiring a transferring apprentice be provided a transcript of related instruction and on-the-job learning, transfer to the same occupation, and sign a new apprenticeship agreement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Changes are described as non-substantive clarifications of existing §29.5(b)(13)(i)-(iii).

rubrics_metrics.name: Recordkeeping by sponsors and participating employers (§29.8(a)(22))
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards must require maintenance of apprenticeship records by program sponsors and participating employers, consistent with the recordkeeping provisions in proposed §29.18.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adding participating employers allows collection of data such as whether the apprentice was hired, interim credentials earned, apprentice's wage upon hire, etc. Proposed change clarifies that specified records must be maintained for five years. Enhancements are intended to support a comprehensive national dataset and data-driven oversight.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adherence to EEO requirements (§29.8(a)(23))
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards must include a statement that the program will be conducted, operated, and administered in conformity with 29 CFR part 30 or, if applicable, an approved State EEO plan.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Replicates existing requirement at §29.5(b)(21) to ensure nondiscriminatory administration of programs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintaining a safe and inclusive workplace (§29.8(a)(24))
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards would address maintaining a safe and inclusive workplace.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chunk indicates a proposed provision but provides no further detail in this excerpt; likely intended to complement other safety, accessibility, and EEO-related requirements described above.
